sections.heading: Overshoot from slow voltage loop
sections.text: Full-bridge overshoot: same as other isolated topologies — the voltage loop is too slow. With phase-shift modulation, the effective duty cycle changes nonlinearly with phase shift. Use peak-current-mode control for linearizing the power transfer.

sections.heading: Slow settling from phase-shift range
sections.text: If the full-bridge settles slowly, check: (1) Is the phase-shift range adequate? At light load, the minimum phase shift may be too large, causing over-regulation. (2) Is the current loop fast enough? f_ci ~ fsw/5.

sections.heading: Excess ripple from leakage inductance
sections.text: Leakage inductance causes ringing on the primary during switching transitions. Add snubbers or use the parasitic ringing for ZVS (phase-shift full-bridge). Output ripple is set by the output inductor and capacitor — recheck passives.

sections.heading: ZVS loss at light load
sections.text: Phase-shift full-bridge loses ZVS at light load because the energy stored in the leakage inductance is insufficient to charge/discharge the MOSFET capacitances. The body diode conduction increases losses. Consider adaptive dead-time or burst mode at light load.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the full-bridge fails across iterations, consider: (1) PSFB (phase-shifted full-bridge) for better ZVS range, (2) resonant transition for wider ZVS, (3) LLC if the conversion ratio is fixed.
